xlsx-formula-editing.name: xlsx-formula-editing
key_points: `=` in formulas: In the XML `<f>` element, the formula is stored without the leading `=`. openpyxl re-adds it when reading.
Element order: `<f>` must come before `<v>` within each `<c>` element for valid OOXML.
Shared strings: If you're editing text cells, they may use the `t="s"` attribute referencing sharedStrings.xml. Number cells store values directly in `<v>`.
Zip path: Sheet files live at `xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml` inside the xlsx, not at the root.

PPTX embedded Excel: When the xlsx is embedded in a PPTX, it's at `ppt/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx`. You must: unpack PPTX → modify xlsx → repack xlsx → repack PPTX. Use the powerpoint skill's `unpack.py` and `pack.py` for the PPTX layer.

skillsbench-task-execution.name: skillsbench-task-execution
key_points: When a task involves parsing a directed graph (e.g., dialogue trees, state machines) and edges point to a sink like "End", do NOT add the sink as a node in your output graph. Many reachability tests' BFS traverse edges but skip the sink node when enqueuing, so adding the sink makes it appear "unreachable" and triggers a false failure. Treat the sink as an external node referenced by edges only.
Always read the `environment/Dockerfile` to find the actual `WORKDIR`, `COPY`, and `mkdir` paths — don't assume `/root/`
Distance must never go below 5m (safety constraint)
Important: Not all tasks support local verification. There are two categories:
Always test with `ldd` after setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — if no "not found" lines appear, it will work
Always run `ldd` on the binary *after* setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to verify all deps resolve before wasting a simulation iteration

Important: The BugSwarm `get_diff` endpoint is the fastest path to the solution. Use it to understand the fix class, then derive the solution yourself (don't just copy the diff — the task requires analysis and applying changes).
